title: Great Plains: named routes, endpoints and rights
lede: Prioritize OPTK Omaha–Denver capacity, Illinois–Indiana enterprise access and a priced Michigan handoff. The evidence now reaches named facilities; connection rights and route economics are the next gate.
scope: Public-source review as of September 20, 2026. Exchange and facility listings are dated observations, not certified live circuits. Proposed structures and rankings are analytical judgments. Residential FCC availability is not used as proof of enterprise route reach.

sections.title: Start with three commercial tests
paragraphs: The first screen is a priced service or rights transaction at exact endpoints. A whole-company acquisition becomes attractive only if it adds transferable customer margin or network control beyond the same-endpoint wholesale alternative. These are proposed diligence priorities, not indications of seller willingness or buyer mandate.

rows: 1. OPTK Omaha–Denver capacity
GPC and OPTK have published OmahaIX entries and advertise common facilities. A facility case study identifies a completed OPTK Denver–Omaha path. [NE_A03] [NE_A05] [NE_A06] [NE_A21]
No useful spare capacity, inadequate rights, or the proposed backup shares the existing path. No bilateral GPC–OPTK NNI is verified.
2. Joink / NITCO / Metro IL–IN access
Named exchange and facility records create specific handoff candidates. Require enterprise buildings and off-net invoices to establish incremental margin. [IM_P01] [IM_P02] [IM_P03] [IM_P04]
A shared last-mile supplier, unassignable municipal rights, or gap construction absorbs the margin. Registry co-listing is self-reported.
3. 123NET Michigan access via Chicago

GPC names 350 Cermak on its 400G-capable route; 123NET lists Chicago peering locations. Detroit endpoints and a completed Southfield–Bay City installation make a defined access test possible. [MI15] [MI16] [MI05]
No economical accepted handoff, unavailable capacity, or shared-risk paths. Sponsor proximity does not remove minority, fund, creditor or regulatory requirements.

sections.title: What the buyer actually has
paragraphs: Rightfiber announced the completed Ritter / Great Plains combination on September 2, 2026. Retain the legacy GPC and Ritter network evidence separately until exact operational integration is demonstrated. [NE_A22]

GPC explicitly names 1623 Farnam, Omaha. Its May 31, 2022 release describes a completed 400G-capable service to 1102 Grand. The facility operator places 1102 Grand in Kansas City, Missouri; the GPC release’s Kansas reference is a geographical error. A named service does not disclose the exact underlying fiber path. [NE_A01] [NE_A17] [NE_A16]

OmahaIX’s current published roster lists both GPC AS13807 and OPTK AS16851 at 100G with route-server participation. That improves the starting evidence beyond a city dot. It still does not establish a bilateral NNI, cross-connect contract, current traffic or available capacity. [NE_A03]

GPC’s operator-maintained PeeringDB record also advertises specific facilities in Denver, Des Moines, Indianapolis and Sioux City. Facility and peering update dates differ; advertised presence is not a live circuit or title check. [NE_A05] [NE_A07]

sections.title: Keep acquired assets and rights straight

rows: Pinpoint / Cambridge
GPC closed the purchase of two Pinpoint backbone business units on February 11, 2016; the release reported 1,200 fiber miles, including 135 in Omaha. [NE_A08]

Do not count the sold backbone as a new target. Reconcile remaining entities, current ASNs, later builds, local customers and retained rights. The Cambridge grant attachment inventories a proposed project, not every current asset. [NE_A09]
OPTK / NebraskaLink
Current branding and regulator evidence support NebraskaLink Holdings d/b/a OPTK. Historical filings describe owned and leased facilities. [NE_A12] [NE_A14]
The 2021 ownership percentages are historical. Obtain today’s cap table, route-specific title/lease/IRU terms and transfer consents. No full current cap table is established.
Metro / Clearwave assets

FCC authorization is March 12, 2026. Counsel’s June 24 financing announcement says acquired Clearwave assets entered collateral for financing closed June 23, supporting completed acquisition by then. [IM_P08] [IM_P09] [IM_P10]

Exact acquisition closing date, transferred legal entities, asset schedule and lien releases remain to be confirmed. Existing Metro facility listings do not prove the acquired spans reach those demarcs.
Bluebird / Everstream

Bluebird announced completed purchase on March 6, 2026. Management’s connected-network and orderability statements are company claims. Historical OpCo/PropCo and Uniti IRU arrangements remain material. [IM_P11] [IM_P12] [IM_P13] [IM_P14]
Map rights by span and legal entity, including amendments and transaction / Chapter 11 treatment. No fee title, assignability, onward IRU grant or carve-out availability is assumed.
123NET / Rightfiber / Omni

Grain’s majority 123NET investment closed in July 2024. Sponsor relationship is a route for coordination; 123NET remains a separate perimeter. Omni’s listed DET-IX ports do not make Omni part of Rightfiber. [MI01] [MI02] [MI03] [MI04]
Use arm’s-length pricing and verify minority, fund, lender and regulatory consent. No automatic transfer or seller willingness.
InterCarrier vs Indiana Fiber Network
GPC’s 2019 completed acquisition was InterCarrier Networks; ETC followed in 2020. [H_P09] [H_P10]
Keep InterCarrier Networks distinct from Indiana Fiber Network / Intelligent Fiber Network, the separately identified Zayo transaction. Do not map entities by acronym alone.

sections.title: Separate planned middle mile from operating capacity
paragraphs: Bluebird / Missouri Network Alliance’s named project corridors are Jefferson City–Washington, Washington–Rolla, Rolla–Strafford and Springfield–Carthage. NTIA’s 2023 award describes 325 planned Missouri miles; the 2024 RFP uses 330. Planned non-grant connectors through Strafford and Springfield are not accepted end-to-end continuity. Obtain scope reconciliation, completion certificates and service-ready notices. [IM_P15] [IM_P16]

123NET and PFN announced completion of the approximately 130-mile Southfield–Bay City installation in February 2025. Completion supports that named corridor, but not a GPC interconnection, spare capacity, exclusive ownership or a new route into every nearby city. [MI15]

Rightfiber markets Seagoville separately from its Coming Soon lists for Ennis, Forney, Mabank and Terrell. Dallas-area Gigabit POPs are separate partner endpoints; no Rightfiber / GPC presence at those facilities is established by the reviewed sources. [RF01] [GF01]

sections.title: The evidence needed before paying an ownership premium
bullets: Exact A/Z buildings, meet-me rooms and accepted demarcations; live circuit identifiers, capacity, LOA/CFA and current local-versus-remote exchange arrangements.

As-built route and shared-risk groups: ducts, bridges, crossings, splice points, regeneration, entrances, power and underlying third-party carriers. A different corporate owner does not prove diversity.
Cable, conduit, easement, lease and IRU ownership or use rights by span; remaining terms, maintenance obligations, grant constraints, liens and assignment consents.

Signed enterprise demand, avoidable off-net cost, recurring contribution after every leased gap, connection capex and replacement cost. Price wholesale, IRU and ownership at the same endpoints and service level.
A proposed route fails the investment test if useful rights cannot be conveyed, required gap capex consumes the margin, or a contract captures the same benefit at lower total cost.

routeRows.counterparty: NebraskaLink Holdings, LLC d/b/a OPTK Networks
routeRows.geography: 1623 Farnam, Omaha to Denver; CoreSite DE1 is a common advertised Denver facility candidate, not a verified endpoint of the specific marketed OPTK path
routeRows.evidence: OmahaIX publishes separate GPC and OPTK participant ports; both advertise 1623 Farnam and CoreSite DE1 in PeeringDB. The facility case study reports a completed OPTK Denver-Omaha path. No bilateral GPC-OPTK NNI or exact path to DE1 is verified. [NE_A03] [NE_A05] [NE_A06] [NE_A07] [NE_A11] [NE_A12] [NE_A13] [NE_A14] [NE_A15] [NE_A21]
routeRows.limits: Public records establish a historical mixed facilities model and an order-based PDR framework. Current span title, lease/IRU term, capacity availability and assignability are unknown. Approval is for diligence, not a new-endpoint or diversity claim. Do not count the same OPTK opportunity as separate Omaha and Denver acquisitions.
routeRows.nextAsk: Request current bilateral service schedule, LOA/CFA, circuit and demarcation IDs; map Denver endpoint; obtain span KMZ, shared-risk crossings, entrances, fiber/IRU/lease schedule, spare capacity, consent rules and binding service quote.

routeRows.geography: Company-described builds from Fort Morgan to Scottsbluff and Grand Island, with La Junta also named; exact facility/splice endpoints unknown
routeRows.evidence: Company history places the named build in 2016-2018; current Fiber site markets relevant wholesale products. No GPC-Viaero connection is verified. [NE_A19] [NE_A20]
routeRows.limits: Viaero markets owned/operated fiber and a wholesale product portfolio. No specific cable, ROW, IRU, capacity or carve-out rights have been verified. Route diversity, exact tie point, unencumbered spare fiber and seller willingness remain unknown. The city sequence is not as-built geometry.
routeRows.nextAsk: Require named GPC handoff and site survey, route KMZ, shared-risk comparison, fiber allocation and wireless commitments, title/ROW chain and priced contract options.

routeRows.counterparty: Pinpoint Holdings, Pinpoint Communications and Cambridge Telephone, subject to current entity verification
routeRows.geography: Cambridge/Bartley and other currently marketed southwest Nebraska business/residential communities; Omaha IX participation is a separate identity/right-verification lead
routeRows.evidence: Current Pinpoint site markets named local services. The proposed grant-asset perimeter is identified in a 2023 filing. No continuous transport corridor, completed Bartley North build or GPC handoff is certified here. [NE_A08] [NE_A09] [NE_A18] [NE_A03] [NE_A32]
routeRows.limits: The Bartley North attachment names Cambridge as owner of proposed grant-area assets and Pinpoint as reseller under common Pinpoint Holdings ownership. It is not a present full-network title schedule. Weaker route case than OPTK or Viaero. Do not re-acquire on paper the backbone already sold in 2016, or assume all present assets were retained at that time rather than built later.
routeRows.nextAsk: Reconcile sold, excluded, retained and subsequently built assets; verify legal entities/ASNs, current cap table, grant completion/encumbrances, customer mix, on-net enterprise buildings, current backhaul contracts and assignability.

routeRows.geography: FD-IX Indianapolis; 733 W. Henry; Equinix Chicago; 900 Walnut
routeRows.evidence: Self-reported common endpoints only; no bilateral connection established [IM_P01] [IM_P02] [IM_P05]
routeRows.limits: Underlying transport, colocation and strand rights unknown Use as a shortlist for interconnection design; no physical diversity or revenue synergy credit.
routeRows.nextAsk: Confirm exact demarcs, LOA/CFA, circuit design, optical layer, local/remote IX access and shared-risk routes.

routeRows.geography: Equinix Chicago; separate local operating cases in Chesterton and East Chicago
routeRows.evidence: Chicago registry co-listing; no municipal-to-GPC path established [IM_P01] [IM_P03] [IM_P17] [IM_P18]
routeRows.limits: Municipal license/operating roles require current contracts; city owns the East Chicago plant identified in the 2022 record Do not sell this as acquisition of the municipal fiber or name the four unnamed data centers.
routeRows.nextAsk: Review current operating agreements, assignment/termination provisions and path to a named demarc.

routeRows.geography: 350 E. Cermak, Chicago; STLIX / 900 Walnut, St. Louis
routeRows.evidence: Registry co-listings only; no GPC-Metro cross-connect or acquired-span handoff verified [IM_P01] [IM_P04] [IM_P06] [IM_P07] [IM_P08] [IM_P20] [IM_P21]
routeRows.limits: Generic products exist; acquired-span title, collateral and consent perimeter unknown Chicago labels are one address. Acquisition and facility presence must remain separate facts.
routeRows.nextAsk: Obtain post-close asset and lien schedules, A/Z quote, assignment rights and physical shared-risk drawings.

routeRows.geography: Netrality 1102 Grand, Kansas City
routeRows.evidence: Dated ecosystem listing; no bilateral NNI confirmed [IM_P19] [IM_P22]
routeRows.limits: Facility access, bilateral agreement and segment rights remain unverified Existing-facility commercial lead only. No assumed route diversity, available port or ownership.
routeRows.nextAsk: Confirm current suite/MMR and port inventory, exact service endpoints, rights holder and entrance/conduit paths.

routeRows.geography: Jefferson City-Washington; Washington-Rolla; Rolla-Strafford; Springfield-Carthage
routeRows.evidence: Planned project scope; segment completion, acceptance and orderability unknown [IM_P15] [IM_P16]
routeRows.limits: Award/design evidence only; current title and grant/lease constraints unverified Approved as a construction-status diligence list only; no operating-mile, IRU-availability or completed end-to-end continuity claim.
routeRows.nextAsk: Get grant scope reconciliation, span-level acceptance and as-builts, rights register and service-ready notices.

routeRows.geography: FD-IX Indianapolis
routeRows.evidence: Public registry lists a port; no bilateral session or physical route verified [IM_P01] [IM_P23]
routeRows.limits: Transport to exchange and local-versus-remote access unknown The 2020 peering-info timestamp limits freshness; Whitewater route completion was not independently re-audited here.
routeRows.nextAsk: Confirm IX access and live status; retain recorded completion gap pending grant closeout.

routeRows.geography: 123NET DC1, 24700 Northwestern Hwy, Southfield, MI 48075; DET-IX core switch fabric at DC1
routeRows.evidence: DC1 and the DET-IX core are operating, named endpoints. 123NET and Omni Fiber have listed exchange ports. [MI04] [MI05] [MI06] [MI13]
routeRows.limits: The DET-IX roster generated on 2026-09-20 contains no Great Plains Communications or Rightfiber name match. The public record therefore does not prove a Rightfiber/GPC port, peering session, NNI, cross-connect or route into DC1. Do not lead with ownership. Compare the priced port and transport solution against the incremental margin and control that an asset transfer would add.
routeRows.nextAsk: Request a budgetary 10G and 100G port and cross-connect package at DC1, including LOA/CFA, install interval, recurring cost, available capacity, route diversity and handoff demarcation. In parallel, ask whether GPC ASNs can join DET-IX directly or through a transport reseller. Stop if: No assignable rack or port capacity, no economical path from an existing GPC POP, or both A/Z paths share the same entrance, duct or upstream carrier.

routeRows.geography: 123NET DC2, 24275 Northwestern Hwy, Southfield, MI 48075; 123NET DC3, 24245 Northwestern Hwy, Southfield, MI 48075
routeRows.evidence: DC2 and DC3 are named 123NET facilities and DET-IX locations. [MI04] [MI07] [MI08]
routeRows.limits: Three nearby Southfield buildings do not establish physical path diversity. The reviewed sources do not establish that GPC enters either building or that an A/Z pair avoids shared Northwestern Highway conduit, power or upstream risks. Facility or fiber ownership is unnecessary unless the dual-site test proves durable demand and third-party terms prevent economical scale.
routeRows.nextAsk: Quote one primary cross-connect at DC1 and one backup at DC2 or DC3. Require as-built path, entrance-vault, duct, splice, power and upstream-carrier separation before paying for a second circuit. Stop if: The two circuits share a building entrance, conduit segment, splice case, power dependency or single upstream carrier.

routeRows.geography: 365 Data Centers, 24660 Lahser Rd, Southfield, MI 48033; EdgeConneX DET01, 21005 Lahser Rd, Building 4, Southfield, MI 48033
routeRows.evidence: 123NET/DET-IX can be reached at identified third-party Southfield colocation facilities. [MI04] [MI09] [MI10]
routeRows.limits: Carrier lists show potential counterparties, not a contracted GPC path. A DET-IX location is not proof that every member is present at every facility or that the exchange extension is physically diverse from DC1. No ownership case is established by the reviewed sources. These are third-party facilities whose value is access and optionality.
routeRows.nextAsk: Ask existing GPC upstreams or carrier partners for a protected Ethernet or wavelength quote into EdgeConneX DET01 and 365 Southfield, then compare the two LOA/CFA and shared-risk groups. Order a short-term port only where an existing GPC carrier already has a usable demarcation. Stop if: No current carrier can deliver to GPC at an economic rate, or both quotes backhaul over the same Chicago-to-Detroit or Southfield metro span.

routeRows.geography: DET-IX meet-me room, 100 Renaissance Center, Detroit, MI
routeRows.evidence: The exchange has a named downtown Detroit endpoint. [MI04]
routeRows.limits: The public source does not identify a GPC port, a 123NET-owned entrance, any enterprise customer, or a complete path from 100 Renaissance Center to a Rightfiber POP. No acquisition or asset-transfer case exists on public evidence. Use the meet-me room as a demand-led enterprise handoff.
routeRows.nextAsk: Request the DET-IX node's carrier list, MMR operator, LOA/CFA process, port inventory and 123NET transport quote back to DC1. Test one named enterprise requirement before any broader downtown build. Stop if: No Rightfiber customer demand, no GPC-reachable carrier at the MMR, or landlord and riser costs make the endpoint inferior to DC1.

routeRows.geography: 123NET DC4, 400 76th Street SW, Suite 12, Byron Center, MI 49315; Grand Rapids Internet Exchange access at DC4
routeRows.evidence: DC4 is an operating 123NET data center with multiple named on-site carriers. [MI11] [MI12] [MI14]
routeRows.limits: The reviewed sources do not establish that GPC reaches DC4, that GRR-IX has a GPC/Rightfiber port, or that DC4 is physically diverse from a Southfield service path. Keep ownership as a later portfolio question. First prove that DC4 produces incremental enterprise or carrier revenue rather than duplicating third-party access.
routeRows.nextAsk: Obtain a 10G and 100G protected transport quote from GPC's Chicago or Indianapolis carrier POP to DC4 through two separately identified carriers. Require the current GRR-IX roster and route-level shared-risk analysis. Stop if: No qualified enterprise demand, no second physical path, or transport cost exceeds a direct third-party carrier solution.

routeRows.geography: Southfield; Beverly Hills; Birmingham; Bloomfield; Pontiac; Waterford; Clarkston; Davisburg; Holly; Fenton; Grand Blanc; Flint; Clio; Birch Run; Bridgeport; Saginaw; Bay City
routeRows.evidence: The 123NET/PFN corridor is described as completed and connected into the partners' networks and DET-IX. [MI13] [MI15]
routeRows.limits: The joint announcement does not establish which party owns each span, whether Rightfiber can use it, or whether any named GPC facility has a physical connection to the route. Any ownership discussion must wait for a joint-asset schedule and PFN consent analysis. The public record supports partnership before control.
routeRows.nextAsk: Select one A/Z requirement between DC1 and a named Flint, Saginaw or Bay City customer location. Request priced lit wavelength, Ethernet and dark-fiber/IRU alternatives with full route, pair, restoration and assignment schedules. Stop if: No continuous assignable right across both partners, no customer-backed lateral, insufficient capacity, or shared restoration and route risks erase diversity.

routeRows.geography: 123NET DC1/DC2/DC3/DC4 peering reference to Equinix Chicago; GPC 350 Cermak Rd data-center endpoint, Chicago; GPC 1623 Farnam endpoint, Omaha
routeRows.evidence: Each network separately markets Chicago access. [MI04] [MI05] [MI07] [MI08] [MI11] [MI16] [MI17] [MI18]
routeRows.limits: No reviewed source establishes that 123NET and GPC occupy the same Chicago facility or meet-me room, have a cross-connect, exchange traffic, or offer an end-to-end Michigan-to-GPC path. Equinix Chicago must not be assumed to mean 350 Cermak without an LOA/CFA or facility schedule. A working NNI can capture most near-term value. Ownership should be considered only if traffic volume, gross margin and route control justify the added minority, fund, creditor and regulatory complexity.
routeRows.nextAsk: First confirm 123NET's exact Equinix Chicago address and MMR. If it is 350 Cermak, price a cross-connect and 10G/100G NNI. If it is another Chicago building, price a protected metro wavelength between the two MMRs. Benchmark against GPC managed Ethernet, which currently markets up to 100 Gbps and access to more than 29 Midwest data centers and carrier hotels. Stop if: No common building, uneconomic metro extension, unavailable capacity, or a Michigan-to-Chicago route that shares the same carrier and physical risk as the intended backup path.

routeRows.geography: Texarkana, Arkansas and Texas; I-30 transport corridor
routeRows.evidence: Ritter announced a $16 million investment in June 2020, including $12 million for the I-30 transport route and $4 million for the local business market. That release said business-zone availability would begin in July. The current service page markets Texarkana. [RF03] [RF01]
routeRows.limits: No exact A/Z route, Jonesboro connection, specific serviceable building, fiber title or diverse path is established here.
routeRows.nextAsk: Obtain a named enterprise order, current building serviceability, accepted route and demarcation, latency, protection and service quote before assigning incremental revenue.

routeRows.geography: Texarkana-to-Dallas wholesale extension test; 1950 North Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, TX 75207
routeRows.evidence: Texarkana is currently marketed as a legacy Ritter business-fiber market. [RF01] The reviewed sources do not establish a Rightfiber POP at 1950 North Stemmons. Partner POP evidence; the connecting route is hypothetical. Gigabit Fiber lists a GIGAPOP at 1950 Stemmons and names Equinix DA1, DA3 and DA6. Equinix confirms DA1, DA3 and DA6 at the address. No Rightfiber/GPC NNI is evidenced. [RF03] [GF01] [GF02] [DC01]
routeRows.limits: The missing leg from Texarkana to the facility, meet-me-room location, cross-connect availability, route mileage, diversity, optical budget, price and term require diligence.
routeRows.nextAsk: Request a priced 100G wavelength or Ethernet handoff from Gigabit at 1950 North Stemmons to extend Rightfiber's Texarkana enterprise reach into a Dallas carrier hotel. Require accepted A/Z demarcations, current capacity, binding terms and a shared-risk path drawing.

routeRows.geography: Seagoville and the southeast Dallas build cluster; 400 South Akard Street, Dallas, TX 75202
routeRows.evidence: RightFiber said construction was underway with Seagoville first in February 2026, and its current service-area page lists Seagoville outside the Coming Soon section. It offers up to 100 Gbps to businesses at the market level. Seagoville is a marketed buyer service area and DFW1 is a partner POP; the connection between them is hypothetical. Gigabit lists a GIGAPOP at 400 South Akard. DataBank calls DFW1 a carrier hotel with 46 onsite carriers. The reviewed sources do not establish Rightfiber presence at this facility. [RF01] [RF02] [GF01] [GF03] [DC02]
routeRows.limits: A city service-page listing is not a specific enterprise lateral. Building serviceability, route completion, customer-ready date, path diversity, NNI and margin split are unknown.
routeRows.nextAsk: Bundle a Seagoville business Ethernet access circuit with a Gigabit wholesale handoff at DFW1 for Dallas carrier, cloud and colocation access. Require accepted A/Z demarcations, current capacity, binding terms and a shared-risk path drawing.

routeRows.geography: Forney and Terrell, advertised future North Texas markets; 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, TX 75201
routeRows.evidence: Rightfiber's current service-area page places Forney and Terrell in Coming Soon. The reviewed sources establish no completed business network, route or enterprise address for either city. The buyer market is planned and a partner POP is named; their connection is hypothetical. Gigabit lists a GIGAPOP at 2323 Bryan. Digital Realty identifies DFW10 at the address, while Equinix identifies DA4 there. Co-location of operators does not establish cross-connect or NNI status. [RF01] [GF01] [GF03] [DC03] [DC04]
routeRows.limits: Coming Soon is not construction completion. The route, delivery milestone, entrance facility, cross-connect, capacity and economics are unknown.
routeRows.nextAsk: Pre-negotiate a conditional managed Ethernet handoff at 2323 Bryan for Forney/Terrell enterprise customers, effective only after customer-ready build milestones. Require accepted A/Z demarcations, current capacity, binding terms and a shared-risk path drawing.

routeRows.geography: Mabank, advertised future North Texas market; 1210 Integrity Drive, Richardson, TX 75081
routeRows.evidence: Rightfiber labels Mabank Coming Soon. The reviewed sources do not establish a completed route or customer-ready premise. The buyer market is planned and a partner POP is named; their connection is hypothetical. Gigabit lists a GIGAPOP at 1210 Integrity Way; Digital Realty's current DFW18 page uses 1210 Integrity Drive. The street-suffix difference should be reconciled before contracting. [RF01] [GF01] [DC05]
routeRows.limits: No buyer route, on-net building, cross-connect, latency, diverse entrance or service date is established. Do not use the facility's power and space scale as evidence of network demand.
routeRows.nextAsk: Test a customer-backed managed Ethernet circuit from Mabank to DFW18 for private-cloud or disaster-recovery access. Require accepted A/Z demarcations, current capacity, binding terms and a shared-risk path drawing.

routeRows.geography: Ennis, advertised future North Texas market, and a north-DFW carrier campus test; 8375 Dominion Parkway, Plano, TX 75024
routeRows.evidence: Rightfiber labels Ennis Coming Soon. The reviewed sources do not establish a completed Ennis-to-Dallas or Ennis-to-Plano path. The buyer market is planned and a partner POP is named; their connection is hypothetical. Gigabit lists a GIGAPOP at 8375 Dominion Parkway. DataBank identifies DFW3 and DFW8 at the address, with 47 onsite carriers on its current campus page. No Rightfiber/GPC presence is evidenced. [RF01] [GF01] [GF02] [GF03] [DC06]
routeRows.limits: This is the longest and weakest geographic hypothesis in the screen. The reviewed sources do not establish the proposed route, and Gigabit's general underground-backbone or diversity marketing cannot substitute for a path diagram.
routeRows.nextAsk: Seek a demand-triggered dark-fiber IRU or managed wavelength to the Plano campus for an Ennis enterprise anchor, subject to a route survey and two-entry-path proof. Require accepted A/Z demarcations, current capacity, binding terms and a shared-risk path drawing.
